subject: Biotechnology
title: DNA Origami Nanostructures
description: A quick, practical guide to DNA Origami Nanostructures.

hook.text: Fold DNA like paper — DNA origami creates nanostructures with precise shapes for drug delivery and molecular machines.

buildup.text: A long scaffold strand is folded by short staple strands — each staple binds specific regions, forcing the desired shape.

discovery.text: DNA nanorobots open in response to cancer cell markers — releasing drug payloads directly at tumor sites.

twist.text: DNA structures degrade in blood within hours — chemical modifications and coatings extend survival for drug delivery.

climax.text: DNA origami templates electronic circuits — biological self-assembly builds structures smaller than lithography can etch.

punchline.text: Fold DNA into anything — DNA origami builds at the nanoscale with atomic precision.

quiz.question: How do DNA nanorobots target cancer cells?
options: They are injected directly into the tumor during surgery
They recognize cancer cell surface markers and open to release drug payloads specifically at tumor sites
They replace cancer cell DNA with healthy DNA sequences
